messages.content: You are one member of a parallel architecture inquiry. Return only the contracted JSON. Produce executable mechanisms, APIs, state transitions, and verification rules; do not propose organizational process or prose-only governance.

Evidence: 84 Claude sessions in five days manually performed environment diagnosis, repository archaeology, architecture reconstruction, research synthesis, Lean proof work, refactors, tests, memory/skill creation, and repeated failure analysis. A transcript audit counted 2,067 direct mutations versus 190 subagent dispatches and about 30% human corrections. Prior harness research specifies carrier adapters with zero substrate intelligence, append-only prompt/tool/result capture, projected memory/context, deterministic tools, governed consolidation only after results, session heartbeats, work claim/settle, and context-compaction continuity. The existing free-compute-dev seed has deterministic resolver -> context -> model edit -> apply -> test -> feedback rounds -> expensive escalation, but only one task and no autonomous intake/decomposition/fanout/tool navigation/isolation/integration/memory. The existing LISS cheapest-sufficient fabric just demonstrated 24/24 schema-verified jobs at 24.45 useful jobs/min across Gemini and GitHub Models, with OpenRouter fallback and Claude available. Future volunteer CPU/GPU endpoints can join over Tailscale. The target is a Union-owned software-production fabric that receives territories/problems and keeps observing, decomposing, executing, verifying, integrating, and learning without a Codex or Claude conversation carrying the work.

Your bounded question: Design the intake compiler that turns an informal territory/problem into executable bounded engineering missions without waiting for a human to decompose it.

State what is absent from the current seed, give a concrete design, and name a smallest real vertical slice.

completion.text: {"component":"Intake Compiler","absentMechanism":"The current seed has a single-task loop requiring a human to hand it a pre-decomposed, bounded task. Nothing exists between \"receive informal territory/problem text\" and \"start executing.\" Nothing identifies unknowns (requiring scout missions before build missions), nothing produces a dependency-ordered mission DAG, nothing bounds each mission to single-session scope, nothing writes a machine-runnable verification predicate per mission. The 84-session manual workload is direct evidence: every decomposition step — archaeology, architecture reconstruction, scope bounding, failure analysis — was a human act the fabric must perform autonomously.","design":["Territory Parser stage: one cheap model call with a strict JSON schema prompt that extracts domain, constraints, known artifacts, unknowns[], and a measurable success condition from free-text input, writing the result to a ContextFrame struct. No code emitted here; only structured knowledge about the problem space.","Mission Synthesizer stage: given the ContextFrame, emit a topologically sorted JSON array of Mission objects each carrying: id, type (scout|build|verify|integrate), depends_on[], objective (one imperative sentence), deliverable (kind + path), verification_predicate (shell command exiting 0 on success), budget (max_tokens + model_tier).","Unknown-first ordering rule: every field in ContextFrame.unknowns[] must map to at least one scout mission before any build mission that depends on that knowledge domain. Scout missions write findings to a named context slot; build missions declare consumed slots in context_keys[]. Synthesizer blocks build missions whose consumed slots have no producing scout mission.","Scope bounding enforced by schema, not by instruction: jsonschema validator rejects any mission whose objective contains two or more finite verbs separated by 'and'|'then'|';'. Rejection causes the synthesizer to recursively split and re-emit until every mission is single-action. Bounding is structural, not advisory.","Verification predicate contract: predicate must be derivable from the deliverable field alone — synthesizer templates it from deliverable kind (file existence check, HTTP status assertion, pytest node id). Free-formed predicates are rejected. Executor appends failed predicate stdout to mission context and re-queues with incremented attempt counter.","Append-only artifact discipline: each intake run writes missions/{timestamp}.json once, never mutates it. Executor appends to results/{timestamp}.json. On re-entry, compiler reads the settled set from results/ and skips settled mission ids, making intake idempotent at the run level.","DAG readiness protocol: executor pulls the next mission whose entire depends_on[] set appears in the settled id set and whose context_keys[] are all populated in the context store. No orchestration logic beyond this set-membership check; sorted array plus settled set drives parallel fanout."],"firstVerticalSlice":["Write intake.py: accepts one free-text argument, calls cheapest LISS-available model (Gemini Flash or GitHub Models cheapest tier) with a fixed system prompt and a JSON schema for MissionList, validates the response with jsonschema, exits non-zero on validation failure and prints the error path.","MissionList schema requires: missions[] non-empty, each mission has id (string), type (enum scout|build|verify|integrate), depends_on (array), objective (string, max 120 chars), deliverable (object with kind and path), verification_predicate (non-empty string), budget.tier (enum cheap|mid|expensive).","Acyclicity check: after schema validation, run topological sort on depends_on graph using Python's graphlib.TopologicalSorter; if a cycle is detected, print the cycle and exit non-zero. Pure Python, no model call.","Smoke test: run intake.py with literal input 'add a health-check endpoint to the inference API' and assert via shell exit code that output is valid, contains at least one build mission, and that mission's verification_predicate contains 'curl' or 'pytest'.","No executor wired yet — the slice proves output shape is correct and machine-runnable before any execution plumbing is added. intake.py is the entire deliverable for this slice."],"failureModes":["Multi-action objective slips schema validation: regex bounding check misses a compound objective phrased without a standard conjunction. Mitigation: add 40-word max as a second gate and flag for human review on rejection rather than silently accepting.","Scout mission result never populates its context slot; downstream build missions start with the unknown unresolved. Mitigation: executor refuses to dispatch any mission whose context_keys[] contain an unpopulated slot, surfacing blocked state rather than proceeding.","Verification predicate tests wrong artifact because template substitution used a default path. Mitigation: integration-test the predicate template against a known deliverable in the smoke test; fail the slice if predicate does not contain the deliverable path string.","Territory so vague that parser emits one catch-all build mission with no derivable verification predicate. Mitigation: assert missions[] >= 1 AND at least one scout mission when unknowns[] is non-empty; halt with structured error naming the unresolved field."],"successMetric":"intake.py, given any free-text territory string of 10–500 words, produces a schema-valid acyclic MissionList in under 30 seconds with zero human intervention; verified by running against 10 diverse inputs sampled from the 84-session backlog and asserting 10/10 jsonschema pass, 10/10 acyclicity, and every build mission's verification_predicate contains the string form of its deliverable path."}

structured_output.absentMechanism: The current seed has a single-task loop requiring a human to hand it a pre-decomposed, bounded task. Nothing exists between "receive informal territory/problem text" and "start executing." Nothing identifies unknowns (requiring scout missions before build missions), nothing produces a dependency-ordered mission DAG, nothing bounds each mission to single-session scope, nothing writes a machine-runnable verification predicate per mission. The 84-session manual workload is direct evidence: every decomposition step — archaeology, architecture reconstruction, scope bounding, failure analysis — was a human act the fabric must perform autonomously.
design: Territory Parser stage: one cheap model call with a strict JSON schema prompt that extracts domain, constraints, known artifacts, unknowns[], and a measurable success condition from free-text input, writing the result to a ContextFrame struct. No code emitted here; only structured knowledge about the problem space.

Mission Synthesizer stage: given the ContextFrame, emit a topologically sorted JSON array of Mission objects each carrying: id, type (scout|build|verify|integrate), depends_on[], objective (one imperative sentence), deliverable (kind + path), verification_predicate (shell command exiting 0 on success), budget (max_tokens + model_tier).

Unknown-first ordering rule: every field in ContextFrame.unknowns[] must map to at least one scout mission before any build mission that depends on that knowledge domain. Scout missions write findings to a named context slot; build missions declare consumed slots in context_keys[]. Synthesizer blocks build missions whose consumed slots have no producing scout mission.

Scope bounding enforced by schema, not by instruction: jsonschema validator rejects any mission whose objective contains two or more finite verbs separated by 'and'|'then'|';'. Rejection causes the synthesizer to recursively split and re-emit until every mission is single-action. Bounding is structural, not advisory.

Verification predicate contract: predicate must be derivable from the deliverable field alone — synthesizer templates it from deliverable kind (file existence check, HTTP status assertion, pytest node id). Free-formed predicates are rejected. Executor appends failed predicate stdout to mission context and re-queues with incremented attempt counter.

Append-only artifact discipline: each intake run writes missions/{timestamp}.json once, never mutates it. Executor appends to results/{timestamp}.json. On re-entry, compiler reads the settled set from results/ and skips settled mission ids, making intake idempotent at the run level.

DAG readiness protocol: executor pulls the next mission whose entire depends_on[] set appears in the settled id set and whose context_keys[] are all populated in the context store. No orchestration logic beyond this set-membership check; sorted array plus settled set drives parallel fanout.
firstVerticalSlice: Write intake.py: accepts one free-text argument, calls cheapest LISS-available model (Gemini Flash or GitHub Models cheapest tier) with a fixed system prompt and a JSON schema for MissionList, validates the response with jsonschema, exits non-zero on validation failure and prints the error path.

MissionList schema requires: missions[] non-empty, each mission has id (string), type (enum scout|build|verify|integrate), depends_on (array), objective (string, max 120 chars), deliverable (object with kind and path), verification_predicate (non-empty string), budget.tier (enum cheap|mid|expensive).

Acyclicity check: after schema validation, run topological sort on depends_on graph using Python's graphlib.TopologicalSorter; if a cycle is detected, print the cycle and exit non-zero. Pure Python, no model call.

Smoke test: run intake.py with literal input 'add a health-check endpoint to the inference API' and assert via shell exit code that output is valid, contains at least one build mission, and that mission's verification_predicate contains 'curl' or 'pytest'.
No executor wired yet — the slice proves output shape is correct and machine-runnable before any execution plumbing is added. intake.py is the entire deliverable for this slice.
failureModes: Multi-action objective slips schema validation: regex bounding check misses a compound objective phrased without a standard conjunction. Mitigation: add 40-word max as a second gate and flag for human review on rejection rather than silently accepting.

Scout mission result never populates its context slot; downstream build missions start with the unknown unresolved. Mitigation: executor refuses to dispatch any mission whose context_keys[] contain an unpopulated slot, surfacing blocked state rather than proceeding.

Verification predicate tests wrong artifact because template substitution used a default path. Mitigation: integration-test the predicate template against a known deliverable in the smoke test; fail the slice if predicate does not contain the deliverable path string.

Territory so vague that parser emits one catch-all build mission with no derivable verification predicate. Mitigation: assert missions[] >= 1 AND at least one scout mission when unknowns[] is non-empty; halt with structured error naming the unresolved field.
structured_output.successMetric: intake.py, given any free-text territory string of 10–500 words, produces a schema-valid acyclic MissionList in under 30 seconds with zero human intervention; verified by running against 10 diverse inputs sampled from the 84-session backlog and asserting 10/10 jsonschema pass, 10/10 acyclicity, and every build mission's verification_predicate contains the string form of its deliverable path.
